title: Gentle Exercises for a Sore or Stiff Shoulder
intro: A stiff shoulder usually feels better with slow movements in a range that doesn't hurt. You can do the moves below at home or in the office, no equipment needed.
muscles: The muscles around the shoulder joint, shoulder blades (scapula), lower neck and chest. The focus is on movement and posture, not lifting heavy.
steps: Sit or stand up straight. Slowly roll your shoulders backwards 10 times, then forwards 10 times.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together like you're pinching a pencil between them. Hold for 3 seconds, then release. Do this 10 times.
Bend forward slightly with one hand supported on a table. Let the other arm hang down and slowly swing it in small circles for 30 seconds (pendulum).
Stand facing a wall. Slowly walk your fingers up the wall as high as feels comfortable, hold for 5 seconds, then come down. Do this 5-8 times.
Place one hand on the opposite shoulder. Use your other hand to gently push the elbow until you feel a light stretch. Hold for 15 seconds on each side.
mistakes: Lifting your shoulders up towards your ears while moving. Keep your shoulders low and relaxed.
Forcing your arm up past the point of pain. Stay within a comfortable range. It will improve slowly.
Only doing it once a week. A stiff shoulder usually prefers small, frequent movements, for example a few minutes every day.
easier: Do only the shoulder rolls and shoulder blade squeezes, while sitting down. Reduce the range and the number of reps.
harder: Add more reps, or do half wall push-ups (hands on the wall, bend your elbows slightly) 8-10 times if there's no pain.
dose: 1-2 sets of each move, once or twice a day, 5-7 days a week. Each session takes about 5-10 minutes.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or weakness spreading down your arm. See a doctor if your shoulder hurts after a fall, you can't lift your arm at all, it's swollen, or the shoulder pain comes with chest pain or shortness of breath.

faq.q: Why does my shoulder get stiff after working at the computer?
faq.a: Sitting for long periods with your shoulders hunched forward can make the muscles tired and tense. Try adjusting your screen height, sit up straight, and do shoulder rolls every hour.

faq.q: Can I use a water bottle as a weight?
faq.a: Yes, but only once the moves without weight feel easy and there's no pain. Start with a small bottle and slow movements.

faq.q: How long until my shoulder feels better?
faq.a: Everyone is different. If there's still no change after 2-3 weeks of gentle exercise, or it's getting worse, it's best to see a doctor or physiotherapist for an assessment.
